worksheet.title: Fix the Mix-Up
worksheet.subtitle: Find the mistake and fix it
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the one card that is wrong and fix it.

parts.title: Bit made a mistake
parts.text: Bit was making a pattern, but one card is wrong. Finding and fixing a mistake is called DEBUGGING. Circle the wrong card, then say what it should be.

parts.title: Watch Bit — this should go ● ▲ ● ▲ …
parts.note: The 5th card is a square ■, but the pattern needs a circle ●. That square is the mix-up.

parts.title: Fix the group
parts.prompt: These should all be circles. Circle the one that does not belong, and say what it should be.

parts.title: Fix the pattern
parts.prompt: This should go ★ ■ ★ ■ … . Circle the card that is wrong, and say what it should be.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: This should go ▲ ● ▲ ● … . Circle the card that is wrong, and say what it should be.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Finding a mistake and fixing it is called debugging. Every coder debugs — even the best ones make mix-ups and then fix them!

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children find the one card that breaks a pattern or group and say what it should be. Spotting and correcting a mistake is debugging — a core computational-thinking skill, and the K-appropriate first taste of fixing code.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children detect and correct an error in a sequence or group.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles the wrong card and names the fix orally.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: build a pattern with blocks, slip in a wrong one, and have children find it.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: read ● ▲ ● ▲ ■ ▲ aloud. 'It should be circle-triangle… but here is a square. That is the mix-up.' Circle it; it should be a circle.
2. GUIDED: do Exercise 1 together — the triangle does not belong in the circle group.
3. YOU TRY: children fix Exercise 2 (last star should be a square) and Exercise 3 (last triangle should be a circle).
4. Connect: 'Every coder debugs — they find a mix-up and fix it. Mistakes are okay; we just fix them.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Model — ● ▲ ● ▲ ■ ▲ → circle the 5th card (■); it should be a circle ●.
Ex 1 — ● ● ▲ ● → circle the ▲; it should be a circle ●.
Ex 2 — ★ ■ ★ ■ ★ ★ → circle the last ★ (6th card); it should be a square ■.
Ex 3 — ▲ ● ▲ ● ▲ ▲ → circle the last ▲ (6th card); it should be a circle ●.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: circling more than one — there is exactly one mix-up; have them read to the end first.
Simplify: use a short 4-card pattern with the mistake near the start.
Extend: have the child make a pattern with a mix-up for a partner to find and fix.
Movement option: clap–stomp–clap–stomp–STOMP — children call out where the mix-up was.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child circles the single wrong card in each item and names the correct shape it should be.
